Tagcast 0.9.0 adds album listening and a full album artist overview alongside
the existing metadata editor, following testing of the two local beta versions.

## What's new

- **Album details:** opening an album shows its tracks, duration, disc information and metadata. Choose **Edit album** when you want to make changes.
- **Album playback:** play an album or start at a chosen track, with automatic advance to the next track. Playback continues while browsing artists, opening other albums or editing metadata.
- **Album artists:** browse cards with photos or fallback initials and album counts. Search names, sort A–Z or Z–A and page through the full collection. Choosing a card opens all albums by that artist and clears album search and filters.
- **Simpler sidebar:** Overview, Albums, Album artists and History remain in the main navigation. The duplicate artist search and list below History have been removed; use the full Album artists overview instead.
- **Development credits:** acknowledge Claude (Anthropic) and ChatGPT / Codex (OpenAI).

## Compatibility and validation

- Album browsing uses compact summaries and loads track details only when needed.
- The existing metadata editor, review before saving, artwork workflow, history and undo remain available. Demo and imported libraries remain local previews.
- Playback uses the existing local streaming proxy and does not report plays or scrobbles. This release adds no shuffle, repeat or additional queue controls.
- Python tests, Ruff, JavaScript parsing, frontend regression tests and start-script checks run in CI on Linux, macOS and Windows. Browser checks use simulated APIs and silent audio.

## Updating

Stop the currently running Tagcast server, download **Source code (zip)** below,
unpack it into a new folder and run the usual start script. The page should show
**0.9.0**. Starting a second copy while the old server is running opens the old
instance instead.

Your account settings and sign-in remain in `~/.tagcast/`, or your configured
`TAGCAST_HOME`. Python 3.11 or newer, or uv, is still required. Tagcast does not
modify local music files.
